Task 9 ANSWERED: there is no ~45 s gap. The denoise phase reconciles exactly across 7 runs.
completed_tasks.progress: wall = encode + command_wait + stream_unhidden_wait + ~0.019s, closing to within 0.019s in all 7 runs (0.005s in the smoke run). Answered by re-reading existing H3_PROFILE logs; no code change, no generation run. The '45 s' was 141 - 96, i.e. the phase wall minus stream_read_seconds, which is CONCURRENT prefetch-thread time and must never be subtracted from a wall. Full working in logs/42-reconciliation.md.

completed_tasks.name: Task 11 ANSWERED: the denoise is GPU-compute bound. root-gpu was under-reporting GPU time by ~10x.
completed_tasks.progress: Found the mechanism in-tree, so no Xcode was needed: MPSGraph calls commitAndContinue inside encodeToCommandBuffer:, committing the root buffer it was handed and returning a fresh one. All six call sites did `gpu.command = command.rootCommandBuffer;`, adopting the new root and DISCARDING the committed one - real GPU work whose timestamps nothing ever summed. Fixed with a counters-only change (retain each retired root, sum GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime, report as mps-gpu; new field so gpu_seconds stays comparable with historical logs). MEASURED: denoise wall 145.832, wait 145.542, root-gpu 10.018, mps-gpu 94.356, gpu-total 104.375, mps-roots 400 (= 200 block visits x 2). So measured GPU busy time is 71.7% of denoise turnaround, not the 6.9% root-gpu implied. 400 buffers carrying 94.4 s were being thrown away. Bit-identity verified: cmp clean vs outputs/h3-egpu-test.mp4, md5 886b40d10c5a83fb01393a4c62bdfcbd. make test: ok 1769 checks. Build clean under -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion.

decisions.decision: No BF16 dtype port for h3.c
decisions.rationale: All 145 native MSL bfloat uses sit inside the M5-only H3_METAL_HAS_TENSOR guard; the 56 portable kernels store BF16 as ushort and accumulate in float. MPSGraph BF16 matmul is bit-exact on gfx1030. The rewrite the brief scoped was unnecessary.

decisions.decision: Gate every discrete-GPU change on hasUnifiedMemory
decisions.rationale: Keeps Apple Silicon behaviour byte-identical to upstream so the patch stays upstreamable.

decisions.decision: Abandoned the matmul rewrite and flash-attention kernel — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-21
decisions.rationale: ORIGINAL: 'Total GPU compute is 17 s of a 240 s run (7%). Two of three peer reviewers ranked this first; measurement retired it.' SUPERSEDED: that 17 s was root-gpu summed across phases, a sum of FLOORS (blocking constraint #1). command_wait puts real turnaround at 162 s of 240 s = 67%. See logs/42-reconciliation.md and remaining task 11. The measurement that retired this was the wrong measurement.

decisions.decision: Rejected mmap + newBufferWithBytesNoCopy as the blit source
decisions.rationale: 32% slower end to end (242.7 -> 321.5 s); sys CPU 125.9 -> 198.6 s from wiring/IOMMU-mapping file pages per block. Kept behind H3_STREAM_MMAP=1 so the result is recorded.

decisions.decision: Committed optimization A despite no end-to-end gain
decisions.rationale: DMA wait -31%, stream -23%, simpler code, bit-identical output. Labelled honestly in the commit message as not delivering the projected win.

decisions.decision: Optimization B retired on measurement, not built.
decisions.rationale: The stream is hidden (unhidden wait 0.025 s of 141 s) and command_wait is demonstrably uncorrelated with stream throughput across a 2.3x range. Reducing bytes moved cannot reclaim time that is not on the critical path.

decisions.decision: Reopened the matmul/flash-attention question that measurement previously retired.
decisions.rationale: It was retired on root-gpu (17 s / 240 s = 7%), a sum of floors. command_wait puts real GPU turnaround at 162 s / 240 s = 67%. The premise was an instance of this project's own blocking constraint #1.

decisions.decision: Metal System Trace route ABANDONED — Xcode cannot be installed on this machine
decisions.rationale: Macmini8,1, Intel Core i7-8700B, x86_64, macOS 15.7.9. Current Xcode requires Apple Silicon, so xctrace is unreachable here permanently — not a download away. Verified Xcode is absent filesystem-wide (spotlight + depth-3 scan), nothing staging in /Applications, no install process. bin/trace-denoise.sh is kept: it is correct and would work on an Apple Silicon box, and its missing-xctrace guard exits cleanly rather than launching a doomed 4-minute run.

decisions.decision: Attribute the MPSGraph time in-tree instead, by keeping the root buffers MPSGraph retires
decisions.rationale: Found the actual mechanism: h3 already encodes MPSGraph into an MPSCommandBuffer wrapping the root buffer (encodeToCommandBuffer:), but MPSGraph calls commitAndContinue internally — it commits that root and hands back a fresh one. All six call sites did `gpu.command = command.rootCommandBuffer;`, adopting the new root and DISCARDING the committed one. Those retired buffers ran real GPU work; the in-order queue makes the submit wait cover them, so their cost is inside command_wait, but nothing ever summed their GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime. That is precisely why root-gpu read 10.1s of a 140.7s phase. No Xcode needed: retain each retired root, sum its timestamps, report it as mps-gpu.

context_notes: Two sessions of perf work were steered by one bad number. root-gpu (gpu_seconds) counted only the root command buffers h3 itself commits, and MPSGraph's commitAndContinue meant 400 buffers per run carrying 94.4 s of GPU work were adopted-and-discarded without ever being counted. That made the GPU look 6.9% busy when it is 71.7% busy, which is what retired the matmul/flash-attention work and what motivated a transfer-side optimization B that could never have paid. Both errors were predicted in advance by this file's own blocking constraint #1 - the fix was to take that constraint literally and go find the missing buffers. Everything is measured now and nothing is being acted on, per owner. Output bit-identical throughout: md5 886b40d10c5a83fb01393a4c62bdfcbd, make test ok 1769 checks.
